newsitem.title: USA: Chicago Stock Exchange committee affirms sanctions.
newsitem.headline: Chicago Stock Exchange committee affirms sanctions.

text.p: The Chicago Stock Exchange said Tuesday its executive committee affirmed a July 1996 decision of its judiciary committee sanctioning a member firm, three of its principals and its trading floor nominee.

Scattered Corp, principals Leon Aaron Greenblatt III, Andrew Alvin Jahelka and Richard Owen Nichols, and floor nominee Laura Bryant had appealed the judiciary committee's decision to uphold a 1995 hearing examiner's judgment against them.
Scattered Corp officials were not available for comment.

The brokerage firm and individuals were fined a total of $6.83 million and hit with other sanctions for allegedly violating "numerous" provisions of the U.S. Securities Exchange Act of 1934, the exchange said.

They were also charged with violating exchange rules regarding illegal short sales, price manipulation, failure to keep adequate records, abuse of position as market maker and excessive trading, the exchange said.

The exchange said it revoked the firm's membership, barred Greenblatt from association with any exchange member, suspended Jahelka and Nichols from association with any member for at least two years and suspended Bryant from membership in the exchange for at least one year.
It said the disciplinary proceeding arose primarily from trading by the firm and individuals in LTV Corp common stock in mid-1993.
